channel.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
channel.description: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

item.title: The first week of testimony wraps in the federal child safety case against Meta
item.description: Week one of the landmark federal child safety trial against Meta is over. Four states are alleging that Meta violated consumer and child data protection laws and hid the risks its platforms risk.
item.content:encoded: Week one of the landmark federal child safety trial against Meta is over. Four states are alleging that Meta violated consumer and child data protection laws and hid the risks its platforms risk.
item.dc:creator: Rachael Myrow

item.title: Harry and Meghan are moving back to the U.K.
item.description: After six years of self-imposed exile, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are leaving California and moving back to the United Kingdom.
item.content:encoded: After six years of self-imposed exile, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex are leaving California and moving back to the United Kingdom.

item.title: So-called 'blue state refugees' have helped turn Florida red
item.description: Conservatives who move from Democratic-run places to Republican-led states are often called blue state refugees. These conservatives have helped reshape the electorate in Florida.

item.title: Wars are happening across the world. Many of them are connected
item.description: All Thing Considered host Mary Louise Kelly speaks with NPR correspondents Tom Bowman and Emily Feng about the ways in which the U.S. war with Iran is connected to other conflicts across the globe.

item.title: What we know about the Penn State cocaine trafficking ring
item.description: One parent and 13 former students have been arrested in a drug trafficking ring at Penn State University. The defendants allegedly transported and distributed large amounts of cocaine.

item.title: Congolese focus on fashion in a weeklong celebration of style and homegrown talent
item.description: In a country better known for conflict and poverty, Congolese celebrated their designer side with the sixth year of DR Congo Fashion week.

item.title: Many recent grads say AI is making it harder to get a job. Economists aren't so sure
item.description: The unemployment rate for 22- to 27-year-olds with higher education degrees is above the national average. Is artificial intelligence to blame?

item.title: The Navajo Nation wants to expand a coal mine. The plan could displace some families
item.description: Coal mining has been a big part of the Navajo Nation's economy for decades. As mines and power plants have been closing, the tribe is trying to expand one of its largest mines.

item.title: The $40 trillion national debt may already be costing you
item.description: The $40 trillion national debt isn't just a number in Washington. It can make borrowing more expensive for everyday Americans, and every realistic plan to bring it down involves tradeoffs.

item.title: As the Tupac murder trial continues, a look back at the cultural moment
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers speaks with Joel Anderson, a host of the podcast Slow Burn, about the Tupac Shakur murder trial and the cultural moment around his murder.
